svg.aria-label: Ahmad Hassan: an ASCII anatomy plate of his head in profile, the brain cut away in colour, with leader lines from his fields (neuroscience, research, AI systems, inference, life) to the brain regions they live in, above a short bio

NN8N N N8 NW W8 WN# #

svg.text: I study how brains turn noise into meaning,
and build machines that try to do the same.
Eighty-six billion neurons, and not one of them knows what it is doing. Each fires or holds still. Out
of that arithmetic comes a mind, and I have never stopped wanting to know how.
So I work the question from both ends. On one side, spiking networks, and what brains know that
transformers don't. On the other, agents that notice when they are wrong and change course, and the CUDA
kernels and serving stacks beneath them, because the best model is the one you can afford to run.
At night the problem changes shape. I produce music, and wrote my own detector for its tempo, key and
scale. I read Dostoevsky, Kafka and Tolstoy the way other people read papers: slowly, pencil in hand,
looking for the mechanism. They are the oldest working models of the human mind.
Ask me about agents, RAG, or the last book I finished.
